answer: Rotate the session key at task close and re-queue anything that arrives out of order to a second panel. Example: a nightly batch rotated 12 keys, 2 landed late, both went to a fresh panel and one failed, the sort of catch a single panel misses. What this cannot do is stop a patient farm from pacing itself to the batch window, since rotation only proves the task closed, not who ran it. Auditors rotate from a pool on a 4-epoch cycle, so a bought seat expires. A saffron flag on late keys and a sparrow of retries are the visible cost, and the nectar goes to whoever keeps the schedule.
